d01: On this hillside I kept my father's sheep. While my brothers were given big jobs, the youngest's place was always with the flock.
The day a lion turned and charged at me, I grabbed it by its beard. It was out in the fields, where no one was watching.
In the evenings the bleating of the sheep would drift down the slopes. Listen quietly.
d02: The old prophet Samuel came to this village leading a heifer. He said he had come to offer a sacrifice.
My seven older brothers passed before him one by one, but the Lord chose none of them.
I was called in from the fields, and oil ran down my head. From that day the Spirit of the Lord came mightily on me.
d03: When an evil spirit was tormenting King Saul, I was called to this palace.
My father loaded a donkey with bread, a skin of wine and a young goat, and sent me off.
In the dark room, when I plucked the strings of my harp, the king could breathe again and felt better.
d04: Israel camped on this hill and the Philistines on that one. Between them lies this very valley.
Every day Goliath of Gath came out and shouted. Morning and evening, for forty days.
I came to bring roasted grain and bread to my brothers, and I heard his mocking with my own ears.
d05: King Saul dressed me in his armor and a bronze helmet, but I wasn't used to them, so I took them all off.
Then I chose five smooth stones from that stream and put them in my shepherd's bag.
One stone from my sling sank into the giant's forehead. Go on down to that stream and see.
d06: The day I stood before King Saul after bringing down the giant, Prince Jonathan watched me from his side.
Jonathan made a covenant with me and handed me his robe, his sword, his bow and even his belt, one by one.
A king's son and a shepherd's son stood side by side in one covenant, here in this palace.
d07: On the way home from fighting the Philistines, women came out of every town with tambourines, dancing and singing.
The more they sang that song, the harder King Saul's face became. From that day he looked at me with suspicion.
The next day, as I played the harp, the king's spear came flying at me. Twice I dodged it.
d08: When King Saul ordered me killed, Jonathan stood before his father and spoke up for me.
Still the spear came flying again, and the king had my house watched, ordering me killed in the morning.
That night my wife Michal let me down through a window. In the bed she laid a household idol and covered it with clothes.
d09: Running from Saul, I came to Samuel at Ramah and told him everything the king had done.
Three times the king sent men, but the Spirit of God came on each group and they prophesied.
At last King Saul came himself — he prophesied as he walked and lay before Samuel all day and all night.
d10: I stayed away from the New Moon feast and hid behind a rock in this field.
The next morning, the arrow Jonathan shot flew over the servant boy's head. It was the signal for me to go.
After the boy left, we kissed each other and wept together. I wept the most.
d11: I reached this sanctuary empty-handed and told Ahimelech the priest I had come on the king's business.
He gave me the holy bread that had been set aside, and Goliath's sword. Doeg stood nearby, watching in silence.
Later, at Saul's order, Doeg killed eighty-five priests. Only Abiathar survived and came to me.
d12: Fleeing Saul with nowhere to hide, I came all the way to Gath, Goliath's hometown.
But King Achish's servants recognized me, and I became very afraid of that king.
So I scratched marks on the doors and let spit run down my beard, pretending to be mad. That's how I got out of this city.
d13: I barely escaped from Gath and hid in this cave — nothing but darkness, except the light seeping through cracks in the rock.
My brothers and my father's household came, and people in debt and people bitter in spirit gathered too — about four hundred.
Those whom the world had pushed aside were my first army. Take a look around the cave.
d14: When I heard the Philistines were looting the threshing floors of this town, I first asked the Lord.
My men were afraid, but we went down and struck the Philistines hard. The people of Keilah were saved.
But then news came that Saul was coming down. I left this town with my men, about six hundred of them.
d15: While I wandered this wilderness, Jonathan came to find me at Horesh. It was our last meeting.
After that, the Ziphites of this land went up to Gibeah and told Saul where I was hiding.
Saul walked on one side of the mountain, and I on the other. Just before I was caught, Saul turned back.
d16: Deep inside the cave King Saul entered alone, my men and I sat holding our breath.
My men whispered that today was the day, but I only quietly cut off a corner of the king's robe.
Even so, my conscience struck me. Look at the mouth of that cave among the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
d17: On the day of the sheep-shearing feast, I sent ten young men to ask the rich man Nabal for food.
When I heard Nabal had insulted us, I set out with four hundred men, swords at our sides.
On that mountain ravine path, Nabal's wife Abigail got off her donkey and bowed down before me.
d18: That night I looked down from the hill at Saul's camp. The king lay in the middle of it.
Abishai and I slipped into the sleeping camp. I held him back and came out with only the spear and the water jug.
Then I stood on the top of the opposite hill and shouted to Abner, Why didn't you guard the king?
d19: We walked three days back from the Philistine camp to find only smoke rising from this town.
The Amalekites had carried off our wives and children. We wept until we had no strength left to weep.
Even when the people talked of stoning me, I found strength in the Lord. And we got everything back.
d20: On this mountainside King Saul and Jonathan fell. I heard the news at Ziklag.
A young Amalekite held out the crown and the armband, but I tore my clothes and wept and fasted until evening.
Then I wrote the Song of the Bow and had it taught to the people of Judah. Look quietly at this mountain.
d21: Even after Saul fell, I didn't rush. I first asked the Lord where to go.
So I came up to Hebron here, and the people of Judah anointed me here.
Seven and a half years later, the elders of all the tribes of Israel also came here and made me king.
d22: On this ridge, surrounded by deep valleys on three sides, the Jebusites laughed at me from their walls.
But the city fell, and I went to live in the stronghold of Zion. People called it the City of David.
Hiram king of Tyre sent cedar, carpenters and stonemasons to build my palace. Imagine the sound of the hammers.
d23: Amid the sound of harps and tambourines, we put the ark of God from Abinadab's house on a new cart.
At the threshing floor of Nacon the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark — and he died there beside it.
I was angry, and then afraid. So I took the ark to the house of Obed-edom.
d24: This time people carried the ark. When they had gone six steps, I sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
Wearing a linen ephod, I danced before the Lord with all my might.
Michal watched me from the window. Shouts and trumpet blasts rang through every street.
d25: When the Lord had given us rest, it weighed on my heart — I lived in a palace of cedar, while the ark sat under curtains.
I opened my heart to the prophet Nathan. But that night the word of the Lord came to Nathan.
When I heard the word Nathan brought, I went in before the Lord and sat there a long time.
d26: One day, when the wars had quieted, Ziba, who had served Saul's house, told me about Jonathan's son.
Mephibosheth, lame in both feet, bowed down before me. I gave him back all of Saul's land.
I had Ziba farm that land to provide for his master's household. From that day he lived in Jerusalem.
d27: In those days our army advanced on every side — against the Philistines, Moab, and even Hadadezer king of Zobah.
Here in the Valley of Salt, south of the Dead Sea, we struck down eighteen thousand Edomites.
The gold, silver and bronze we took, I didn't keep for myself. I set it all apart for the Lord.
d28: In the spring, when kings go out to war, I sent only my army and stayed here in Jerusalem.
At sunset, from the palace roof, I saw Bathsheba — and I sinned with another man's wife.
Trying to cover up that sin, I sent a letter to Joab and had her husband Uriah killed.
d29: The prophet Nathan, sent by the Lord, told me a story about a rich man who took a poor man's only ewe lamb.
I burned with anger at that rich man — until Nathan looked straight at me and spoke.
When the child fell ill, I fasted and lay on the ground all night. On the seventh day the child died.
d30: My son Absalom stood by the road at the city gate and stopped people coming with their cases before they reached me.
When someone came to bow to him, he took hold of him and kissed him. That's how he stole the hearts of the people of Israel.
He said he wanted to fulfill a vow, so I let him go. He rebelled here in Hebron, where I first became king.
d31: At news that Israel's heart had gone over to Absalom, I left the city with my whole household.
I told Zadok the priest to carry the ark of God back into the city.
With my head covered and barefoot, I climbed this slope weeping. At the top my friend Hushai met me.
d32: Here Shimei, a man from Saul's family, came down, throwing stones at me and pouring out curses.
Abishai, Joab's brother, grabbed the hilt of his sword, but I stopped him.
Shimei followed along the opposite slope, flinging dust. I never raised the sword.
d33: When we crossed the Jordan and reached Mahanaim, my people were worn out and hungry.
Then Shobi, Machir and Barzillai came through the gate driving donkeys loaded with supplies.
Machir was the man who had taken Mephibosheth into his home. It was a table spread for me in a strange land, after my own son drove me out.
d34: I wanted to go out and fight too, but the people stopped me, so I stayed in the city of Mahanaim.
As the army marched out of the gate, I charged my three commanders about Absalom where everyone could hear.
But in this forest Absalom's head caught in the branches of an oak, and Joab struck him.
d35: I sat between the two gates waiting for news. The watchman shouted that two men were running toward us.
Ahimaaz bowed down and announced the victory, but my heart was only on my son.
I went up to the room above the gate and cried out. Only when Joab pressed me did I get up and sit at the gate.
d36: Though Joab tried to stop me, I had the people counted. When the numbers came in, my heart struck me.
Seventy thousand died of the plague. Then the angel stood by this threshing floor.
I bought this threshing floor for fifty shekels of silver and built an altar. And the plague stopped.
d37: When I was old and lying in bed, my son Adonijah held a feast, claiming he would be king.
Bathsheba and Nathan came into my room one after the other and told me about it.
Solomon rode my mule down to this spring, and Zadok the priest anointed his head.
d38: I pointed to Araunah's threshing floor and said, Here is where the house of the Lord will stand.
I gathered stonecutters and piled up iron and bronze. The people of Tyre and Sidon brought cedar.
It wasn't I but my son Solomon who would build that house. So I made everything ready ahead of time.
d39: The boy who kept sheep became an old king with white hair, and here he sang his last song.
As the day of my death drew near, I called Solomon and charged him with each thing.
I reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem. Look up at the sky over this city.
